correctness.rationale: Positive-good EFX reduces exactly to L_i≥S_ij−s_ij for a nonempty parallel-edge subbundle owned by j, because deletion of its lightest edge leaves its highest remaining value to i. At a violation, L_j−L_i>s_ij>0. The two loads after moving that edge are a doubly stochastic mixing of the old pair, with parameter s_ij/(L_j−L_i) strictly between 0 and 1. This proves the Lorenz comparison for the entire vector even if the loads cross. The square cost drops by 2s_ij(L_j−L_i−s_ij)>0; finite orientations ensure termination for arbitrary real weights. Fixed total, exact endpoint assignment and majorization give the Schur-objective consequences. In the nonexistence example, vertex 2 has possible load 0,4,8; load 4 forces max at least 7 and min at most 4, and load 8 forces min at most 5 and max at least 8, proving the two cited optima are incomparable and undominated. In the asymmetric example, every split has peak R and the unconstrained minimum is 2. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its bounded integer checks are not the real-weight proof.

value.rationale: The repair preserves every Lorenz lower-tail bound simultaneously from a prescribed allocation without discarding value. This materially strengthens mere existence and transfers to all Schur objectives in a weighted class where a single globally Lorenz-best orientation need not exist. It is not claimed as a polynomial-time optimization algorithm.
